title: Valid Anagram

concept.title: Same letters, same counts
body: Two words are **anagrams** when they use exactly the same letters the same number of times, only in a different order. You can test that without sorting: count the letters of the first word up, and the letters of the second word down. If every counter ends at zero, the words are anagrams.

body: First compare the lengths: words of different length can never be anagrams.

statement: You are given two words of lowercase English letters. Print `yes` if the second word can be made by rearranging the letters of the first, otherwise print `no`.
inputFormat: The first line has the word `s`.
The second line has the word `t`.
hints: Words of different length are never anagrams.
Count the letters of `s` up and the letters of `t` down in one table of 26 counters.
The answer is `yes` only when all counters are zero at the end.

starter.python:
s = input().strip()
t = input().strip()

# Your code here

explanation: Count the letters of `s` up and of `t` down. The words are anagrams exactly when every counter returns to zero.

code.python:
s = input().strip()
t = input().strip()

count = [0] * 26
for ch in s:
    count[ord(ch) - ord("a")] += 1
for ch in t:
    count[ord(ch) - ord("a")] -= 1
print("yes" if len(s) == len(t) and all(c == 0 for c in count) else "no")
